Spreading `undefined` or `null` into an object literal adds nothing and does not throw. So `{ ...(options || {}) }` and `{ ...(options ?? {}) }` give the same object as `{ ...options }`.

This is only true for objects. Spreading `undefined` into an array or into the arguments of a call throws, so `[...(items || [])]` is not reported.

`--fix` removes the fallback.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```js
function request(url, options, extraHeaders) {
  const headers = { accept: "application/json", ...(extraHeaders || {}) };
  return fetch(url, { ...(options ?? {}), headers });
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function request(url, options, extraHeaders) {
  const headers = { accept: "application/json", ...extraHeaders };
  return fetch(url, { ...options, headers });
}

// the fallback has something in it
const settings = { ...(saved || { theme: "light" }) };

// arrays need the fallback
const all = [...(items || [])];
```
